projects.title: KRIVIO AI
projects.description: An AI-assisted business mentor and commerce toolkit for rural Indian artisans, farmers, and self-help groups. KRIVIO combines multilingual voice guidance, an AI image studio, product catalog creation, marketplace-ready exports, wholesale PDF quotations, and shareable storefronts. Built with a React and TypeScript frontend, an Express gateway, Python/FastAPI services, PostgreSQL, and Gemini integrations.
projects.technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Supabase Auth, Gemini, Tailwind CSS

caseStudy.problem: Rural artisans need practical help preparing products for digital selling: photos, descriptions, pricing, and marketplace formats.
caseStudy.contribution: The project brings a React and TypeScript interface together with an Express gateway, Python services, and PostgreSQL-backed business and product workflows.
caseStudy.decisions:
Keep business context attached to product and mentor workflows.
Use structured marketplace exports rather than treating a generated description as a finished listing.
Support voice and regional-language interactions alongside visual editing.
caseStudy.lessons: AI output needs validation and clear user review before it becomes business data. Authentication, account isolation, and predictable export formats are as important as the generation interface.

projects.title: GitaPath
projects.description: A source-grounded Bhagavad Gita guidance platform that connects everyday questions with relevant teachings and chapter-and-verse references. It includes structured AI conversations, a chapter browser, guided learning, reflection journaling, and voice input. The React and TypeScript interface connects to an Express API with Gemini integration and Supabase authentication.
projects.technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, Gemini, Supabase, Tailwind CSS, Vite

caseStudy.problem: People can describe a difficult life situation but may not know which Bhagavad Gita teaching relates to it or how to verify the source.
caseStudy.contribution: The project connects a conversational React interface with structured guidance responses, chapter-and-verse references, learning tools, reflection features, and an Express API.
caseStudy.decisions:
Return structured guidance with source references instead of a single unstructured answer.
Separate scripture knowledge from explanation and reflection.
Provide explicit fallback behavior when an AI or retrieval service is unavailable.
caseStudy.lessons: Source transparency must be visible in the interface. Graceful failure and clear boundaries help make an AI guidance product more dependable than a chat interface alone.

projects.title: TRUVA
projects.description: A package-label scanning and review application with separate consumer and inspector workspaces. TRUVA extracts printed declarations, explains food-label evidence, compares compatible saved products, and presents inspection records for human review. Built with React and TypeScript, a Python/FastAPI inspection API, Gemini vision, RapidOCR, and Supabase Auth. Scan history is stored locally per account; automated findings support review rather than certify compliance.
projects.technologies: React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, Gemini, RapidOCR, Supabase Auth, Tailwind CSS, Capacitor

caseStudy.problem: Packaged-product labels are difficult to inspect and compare, especially when declarations are incomplete or hard to read.
caseStudy.contribution: The project includes consumer and inspector workspaces, image-based label extraction, evidence-led reports, food-label explanations, and comparison of compatible saved products.
caseStudy.decisions:
Keep consumer vision and detailed inspector OCR workflows distinct.
Treat extracted text as evidence for review, not a verified compliance decision.
Withhold comparisons when quantities or units are incompatible; keep browser-local scan history isolated per account.
caseStudy.lessons: Uncertainty is part of the product experience. Incomplete evidence should remain visible, and an automated finding should not be presented as a legal or medical conclusion.
